newsitem.title: USA: Alabama $700 mln highway bonds pass House panel.
newsitem.headline: Alabama $700 mln highway bonds pass House panel.

text.p: Alabama's House Ways and Means Committee unanimously approved Gov. Fob James' $700 million highway bond proposal, a legislative aide said Thursday.
The committee approved the proposal on a voice vote late Wednesday, sending it on to the full House, where it had not yet been scheduled for debate.

The plan would use existing gasoline taxes to pay debt service on the 20-year bonds. It allocates $150 million for resurfacing roads and highways, $150 million for bridge repair and replacements and $81.9 million to be divided among the state's 67 counties for local projects.
The remaining $318 million would fund construction of bypasses around Birmingham, Huntsville, Tuscaloosa, Decatur, Montgomery and Anniston, plus widening of several two-lane highways to four lanes.
